- **self**: Atlas tier-fixed index build limits (9/3)

## How it works

- [statement] A createIndexes request counts as one active user index build even when it builds several indexes. The request shares its memory budget among those indexes; batching therefore avoids additional concurrency slots but does not grant each index a separate full memory budget. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/v8.3/reference/parameters/ · keywords: Atlas tier-fixed index build limits · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation/, https://oneuptime.com/blog/post/2026-03-31-mongodb-tune-maxnumactiveuserindexbuilds/view

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] Atlas customers cannot modify maxIndexBuildMemoryUsageMegabytes: the parameter reference explicitly describes its Atlas values as unchangeable cluster-tier defaults, and the index-creation guide independently repeats the restriction. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23) Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/v8.3/reference/parameters/ ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation/ — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/v8.3/reference/parameters/ · keywords: Atlas tier-fixed index build limits · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation/
- [statement] The v8.3 parameter reference also explicitly says Atlas maxNumActiveUserIndexBuilds uses cluster-tier defaults that customers cannot change. Its nearby startup/runtime setParameter example describes server configurability and must not be read as an Atlas override procedure. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/v8.3/reference/parameters/ · keywords: Atlas tier-fixed index build limits
- [statement] Reaching maxNumActiveUserIndexBuilds blocks additional user index-build requests until active builds drop below the limit; waiting alone does not establish a failed build. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/v8.3/reference/parameters/ · keywords: Atlas tier-fixed index build limits · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation/

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] The index-build memory limit regulates sorter memory and spilling, rather than setting a maximum final index size: replicated index builds can write sorted runs to temporary files under dbpath/_tmp when their memory allowance is reached. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation/ · keywords: Atlas tier-fixed index build limits · also: https://github.com/mongodb/mongo/blob/master/src/mongo/db/index_builds/README.md

## Facts and statements

- [statement] MongoDB engineering issue SERVER-114768 reports that dividing a build memory budget among many indexes can require intermediate spill-range merges and extend build duration. It also reports cases where increasing memory lengthens builds that still spill, so a larger budget is not a universal speed guarantee. This is server-level evidence, not an Atlas policy exception. (low confidence) (verified as of 2025-12-09) — https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-114768 · keywords: Atlas tier-fixed index build limits
- [statement] SERVER-130149 proposes letting a running index build re-read and apply an increased maxIndexBuildMemoryUsageMegabytes after a spill boundary. The ticket describes a current gap: changing the value at runtime does not help a build already trapped in a bad spill pattern. It is unresolved with Fix Version/s None, and the page was last updated Oct 26 2026. Separately, the MongoDB manual says that on Atlas the default values vary by cluster tier and maxIndexBuildMemoryUsageMegabytes cannot be modified; the ticket does not mention Atlas. Sources: https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-130149 ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/v8.3/core/index-creation/ — https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-130149 · keywords: Atlas tier-fixed index build limits
- [statement] On MongoDB Atlas, maxNumActiveUserIndexBuilds uses cluster-tier default values that cannot be changed, so a recipe that changes it through setParameter (which works at runtime or startup on self-managed deployments) must not be assumed to apply on Atlas. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/v8.3/reference/parameters/ — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/v8.3/reference/parameters/ · keywords: Atlas tier-fixed index build limits · also: https://oneuptime.com/blog/post/2026-03-31-mongodb-tune-maxnumactiveuserindexbuilds/view
- [statement] Percona's August 2019 recipe for increasing index-build memory through a configuration file is historical deployment advice, not evidence that current Atlas users can override the managed memory setting. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23) — https://www.percona.com/blog/mongodb-impact-free-index-builds-using-detached-replicaset-nodes/ · keywords: Atlas tier-fixed index build limits · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation/
